Bill.BriefDescription: Creating a water rights confirmation process.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing certainty and clarity in theadministration of water rights; amending RCW 90.03.380; reenacting andamending RCW 90.14.140; adding new sections to chapter 90.03 RCW;adding a new section to chapter 90.44 RCW; adding a new chapter toTitle 90 RCW; creating a new section; and repealing RCW 90.14.130,90.14.160, 90.14.170, 90.14.180, 90.14.190, 90.14.200, 90.14.210,90.14.215, and 90.14.230.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds that the presentwater rights management system is not able to function quickly andefficiently. This is in part due to the variety of types of waterrights, including many water rights based on claims established priorto the creation of a statutory permit process, and uncertainty raisedby court decisions affecting administration of the water code in lightof this variety of rights. Therefore, the legislature declares that the creation of a waterrights confirmation process is critical to the economic viability ofthe state. The goal of this confirmation process is to providecertainty and clarity to water right holders so that the administration p. 1 SB 6734of the water code is more effective and expedient while ensuring thatwater right holders are ensured due process. This process will resultin faster, simpler water right transactions, provide a clarifiedpicture of actual water use, and provide greater certainty as to theeffect of water withdrawals and diversions on stream flow levels. (2) The legislature finds that the present system for determiningthat a water right holder has relinquished or abandoned a water rightcreates disincentives for using water efficiently, and greatlycontributes to the uncertainty in the use of water rights and to theadministration of an effective water management system. Therefore, the legislature declares that this system should bereformed by repealing the current law of relinquishment and byreforming the law of abandonment to create a system that continues torequire continuous beneficial use of water rights, but also providescertainty and flexibility of use for water right holders and statewater managers. (3)(a) The legislature finds that the present provisions of thewater code are ambiguous regarding whether, in accordance with therelinquishment provisions, the mere nonuse of an otherwise valid waterright, without any other action, results in the relinquishment of thatwater right and creates a corresponding right of use in other users.The legislature finds that this ambiguity creates unacceptable levelsof uncertainty for water right holders and state water managers. (b) The legislature further finds that water right holders areentitled to due process under the Washington state Constitution priorto any determination that a water right has relinquished. (c) Therefore, the legislature declares that to ensure an effectiveand efficient transition to a new water rights confirmation process,water rights are not considered relinquished unless determined to be soby a court of competent jurisdiction or an administrative processsubject to judicial review. Any water rights determined to berelinquished by such a court revert to the state for appropriation inaccordance with the water code. (4)(a) The legislature further finds that clear and consistentstandards for changes and transfers are essential to ensure thatexisting water rights are an effective tool for water management. (b) Therefore, the legislature declares that the use of water toirrigate additional acres or supply additional uses may take place as SB 6734 p. 2 long as such a change in the water right does not cause detriment orinjury to any other water right. Additionally, the legislaturedeclares that alternatives to the consumptive use test for waterspreading to additional lands are essential to achieve flexibility. (5)(a) Further, the legislature finds that certain water usesnecessitate greater flexibility and that such uses are currently exemptfrom relinquishment. These uses include: Power development, standbyor reserve water supplies, municipal water supply, federal irrigationprojects, water held in trust, and permits still under development. (b) Therefore, the legislature declares that these water uses, andground water withdrawals exempt from permitting requirements, are notsubject to the water rights confirmation process established in thischapter, unless the holder of the water right elects to subject thatright to the confirmation process.

(1) Within one hundred eighty days of theeffective date of this section, the presiding judge of the water court,or until establishment of a water court, the chief judges of theWashington court of appeals, shall appoint three or more referees asneeded to process water rights under the water rights confirmationprocess established by this chapter. (2) Each referee shall consult with the department of ecology toestablish a water quantity confirmation schedule for each waterresource inventory area of the state. The water rights confirmationprocess created in this chapter must be completed by December 31, 2014,for each water resource inventory area. (3) As of the effective date of this section, all statebased waterrights are subject to the water rights confirmation process, exceptthose rights described in: RCW 90.14.140 (13), (14), (15), (16), (17),and (20); rights exempt from permit requirements under RCW 90.44.050;or permits still under development as described in RCW 90.14.150. (4) Any holder of a right described in RCW 90.14.140 (13), (14),(15), (16), and (17) may choose to have such right confirmed under theprovisions of this chapter. Only the portion of the water rightactually put to beneficial use may be confirmed. Any portion of theright not put to beneficial use may not be confirmed or altered by theconfirmation process established in this chapter. p. 3 SB 6734 (5) Water rights exempt from permit requirements under RCW90.44.050 or permits still under development as described in RCW90.14.150 may be confirmed as to quantity under the provisions of thisact. Only the portion of the water right put to beneficial use may beconfirmed. Any portion of the right not put to beneficial use may notbe confirmed or altered by the confirmation process established in thischapter.

Within ninety days of the effective date ofthis section, the department of ecology shall issue notice to all waterright holders of record through direct mailing and through generalmeans such as newspaper listings and internet postings. The noticeshall include: (1) A brief description of the water rightsconfirmation process created by this chapter; and (2) a request thateach water right holder file current contact information with thedepartment of ecology by July 1, 2005. The contact information must include the current name of the waterright holder, mailing address, telephone numbers, electronic mailaddress, if any, and the tax parcel number of the land to which thewater right is appurtenant. The department of ecology shall make the contact informationavailable to the referees appointed under section 2 of this act.

(1) Each referee shall issue notice ofopportunity to confirm water right quantities to all water rightholders within their assigned jurisdiction. The notice must be madethrough direct mailing to water right holders of record, and throughgeneral means such as newspaper listings and internet postings. Thenotice must also include information related to any technicalassistance available to water right holders to aid in complying withthe provisions of this section. (2) Upon receipt of such a notice, but no later than the timespecified in the notice, all water right holders subject to the waterrights confirmation process shall file a statement of water use withthe referee. The statement of use must include: (a) The highestinstantaneous quantity diverted or withdrawn during the period fromJanuary 1, 1994, through December 31, 2003; (b) the highest annualquantity diverted or withdrawn during the period from January 1, 1994, SB 6734 p. 4 through December 31, 2003; (c) documentation showing that thequantities in (a) and (b) of this subsection were put to beneficialuse; (d) the basis for withdrawal or diversion of water, including thepermit number, certificate number, claim filing number, or otherstatutory authority for the right; and (e) the quantities authorized bythe permit, certificate, claim, or other statutory authority. (3) Documentation under subsection (2)(c) of this section mayinclude power meter records, water meter records, crop and acreagerecords, or any other information to show the quantity of water used.For rights that embody quantities of water use under onetenth of acubic foot per second, the referee shall develop simplified proceduressuch as a checklist for submitting evidence of use. For purposes ofthis section, the highest instantaneous and annual quantities may occurin different years. (4)(a) If the water right holder did not fully exercise a waterright from January 1, 1994, through December 31, 2003, the water rightholder may document the reasons for the nonuse in accordance withsubsections (2) and (3) of this section. If the reason for the nonusewas valid based on RCW 90.14.140, the water right holder may documentthe highest instantaneous quantity and annual quantity put tobeneficial use during the tenyear period immediately preceding theperiod of nonuse. (b) For rights described in RCW 90.14.140 (13), (14), (15), (16),and (17), the instantaneous quantity and annual quantity shall be thehighest quantities put to beneficial use. (5) Those water rights required to be confirmed under section 2(3)of this act, for which a statement of water use is not filed within thetime frame established in subsection (1) of this section, are presumedby the referee to be abandoned. The right must be reported to thewater court if one has been established or the superior court ofcompetent jurisdiction. The court shall annually hear such reports andfind that the rights have been abandoned, unless the water right holdercan prove otherwise.

(1) The referee shall examine thedocumentation submitted for a right under section 4 of this act. Theexamination may only consider if the: p. 5 SB 6734 (a) Right is based on a permit, certificate, or claim filed inaccordance with chapter 90.14 RCW, or other statutory authority; (b) Beneficial use is consistent with the place of use, purpose ofuse, point of diversion or withdrawal, or season of use contained inthe permit, certificate, or claim filed in accordance with chapter90.14 RCW, or other statutory authority; (c) Instantaneous quantity and annual quantity put to beneficialuse are within the quantity authorized by the permit, certificate,claim, or other statutory authority; (d) Reason for the nonuse, if any, was valid based on RCW90.14.140, for water rights addressed in section 4(3) of this act; or (e) Water use in the filing is accurate based on the documentationprovided. (2)(a) By exception and for good cause, the referee may conductfield investigations of a filing to ensure that the requirements ofsubsection (1) of this section are met. The referee may not holdevidentiary hearings. A filing may be further investigated andevidentiary hearings may be held only if the referee's decision isappealed in accordance with subsection (4) of this section, at thedirection of the court. (b) If any filing is incomplete or appears to be inaccurate, thereferee shall return it to the water right holder with an explanationof what additional information is needed. (c) If a water right embodied in a filing requires changes toproperly reflect the current place of use, purpose of use, point ofdiversion or withdrawal, or season of use, the referee shall direct thewater right holder to apply to the department of ecology or a waterconservancy board for such change in accordance with section 11 of thisact. (3) The referee shall issue a record of decision consistent withsections 2 through 4 of this act and twice each month the referee shallpublish a notice reflecting the record of decision of rights confirmedsince issuance of the last notice and provide copies of such a noticeto water right holders in the same water resource inventory area. (4)(a) Any aggrieved water right holder in the same water resourceinventory area or relying on the same source of supply, including theholder of the right for which a record of decision is issued in SB 6734 p. 6 accordance with subsection (3) of this section, may file an appeal ofthe record of decision within thirty days of publication under theprovisions of subsection (3) of this section. (b) The appeal must be filed with the water court if established,or until such time as it is established, with the superior court ofcompetent jurisdiction. (c) For purposes of this section, the department of ecology isdeemed a water right holder for all instream flows established by ruleand trust water rights acquired under the authority of chapter 90.38 or90.42 RCW. This subsection (4)(c) does not affect the authority of thedepartment to regulate existing water rights through the exercise ofregulatory powers granted to the department. (5) If no appeal is filed, the referee shall issue a supersedingdocument reflecting the confirmed quantities. The superseding documentdoes not change the type of underlying right. A superseding claim isissued for a water right claim, a superseding permit is issued for awater right permit, and a superseding certificate is issued for a waterright certificate. (6)(a) If an appeal is filed, the court may only examine whetherthe record of decision is in accordance with the provisions ofsubsection (1) of this section. (b) The burden of proof is on the appellant to show that the recordof decision is inaccurate. (c) The court may conduct evidentiary hearings or fieldinvestigations to supplement the record of decision as needed todetermine if the record of decision is accurate. (d) The decision of the court will serve as the new confirmedquantity for the water right, and the court shall direct the referee toissue the appropriate superceding document in accordance withsubsection (5) of this section.

(1)(a) Except as provided in (d) of thissubsection, once a right has been confirmed in accordance with section4 of this act, the holder of the right must annually submit a notice ofwater use to the department of ecology showing measured or estimatedbeneficial use from the previous year and planned beneficial use of theright during the current calendar year. The notice must be filed byMay 1st of each year. The department of ecology shall mail a reminder p. 7 SB 6734to each holder of a confirmed water right that the annual notice is dueno later than May 1st, and shall provide the holder with a notice cardfor reporting annual use under the right. (b) The annual notice must include how the water will be used, andif any amount of the confirmed right is not planned to be put to use,the water right holder must designate whether such water will betransferred to another user or donated, leased, or sold to the statetrust water right program. (c) Water right holders may file by mail, electronic mail, orthrough the internet. The department of ecology shall keep the noticesand post them on an internet site categorized by watershed. (d) For the purposes of this section, annual notice of water usefor municipal water suppliers means the reports provided to thedepartment of health as required by chapter 70.119A RCW. (2)(a) The department of ecology shall monitor and review submittednotices of water use to ensure the notices are complete and may requirethe water right holder to correct incomplete notices. (b) If a water right holder fails to file an annual notice of wateruse for a confirmed water right for five consecutive years, thedepartment of ecology must notify the water right holder stating thatfailure to file such a notice of water use for ten consecutive yearsconstitutes abandonment of the right. The department of ecology shallannually provide such a notice until a notice of water use is filed inaccordance with subsection (1) of this section. (3) If a notice of water use for a right confirmed under theprovisions of section 4 of this act is not filed for ten consecutiveyears, the right is deemed abandoned on December 31st of the tenthyear. Such a right must be reported to the water court if one has beenestablished or the superior court of competent jurisdiction. The courtshall annually hear such reports and find that the rights have beenabandoned, unless the water right holder can prove that the noticeswere filed.

The department of ecology may issue grantsto public bodies or private associations to provide technicalassistance to water right holders in preparing the initial statement ofwater use or the annual notice of water use, or both. The grants maybe made from funds appropriated by the legislature for that purpose.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 90.03.380 and 2003 c 329 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The right to the use of water which has been applied to abeneficial use in the state shall be and remain appurtenant to the landor place upon which the same is used: PROVIDED, HOWEVER, That theright may be transferred to another or to others and become appurtenantto any other land or place of use without loss of priority of righttheretofore established if such change can be made without detriment orinjury to existing rights. The point of diversion of water forbeneficial use or the purpose of use may be changed, if such change canbe made without detriment or injury to existing rights. ((A change inthe place of use, point of diversion, and/or purpose of use of a waterright to enable irrigation of additional acreage or the addition of newuses may be permitted if such change results in no increase in theannual consumptive quantity of water used under the water right. Forpurposes of this section, "annual consumptive quantity" means theestimated or actual annual amount of water diverted pursuant to thewater right, reduced by the estimated annual amount of return flows,averaged over the two years of greatest use within the most recentfiveyear period of continuous beneficial use of the water right.))Before any transfer of such right to use water or change of the pointof diversion of water or change of purpose of use can be made, anyperson having an interest in the transfer or change, shall file awritten application therefor with the department, and the applicationshall not be granted until notice of the application is published asprovided in RCW 90.03.280. If it shall appear that such transfer orsuch change may be made without injury or detriment to existing rights,the department shall issue to the applicant a certificate in duplicategranting the right for such transfer or for such change of point ofdiversion or of use. The certificate so issued shall be filed and bemade a record with the department and the duplicate certificate issuedto the applicant may be filed with the county auditor in like mannerand with the same effect as provided in the original certificate orpermit to divert water. (2) If an application for change proposes to transfer water rightsfrom one irrigation district to another, the department shall, beforepublication of notice, receive concurrence from each of the irrigation p. 9 SB 6734districts that such transfer or change will not adversely affect theability to deliver water to other landowners or impair the financialintegrity of either of the districts. (3) A change in place of use by an individual water user or usersof water provided by an irrigation district need only receive approvalfor the change from the board of directors of the district if the useof water continues within the irrigation district, and when water isprovided by an irrigation entity that is a member of a board of jointcontrol created under chapter 87.80 RCW, approval need only be receivedfrom the board of joint control if the use of water continues withinthe area of jurisdiction of the joint board and the change can be madewithout detriment or injury to existing rights. (4) This section shall not apply to trust water rights acquired bythe state through the funding of water conservation projects underchapter 90.38 RCW or RCW 90.42.010 through 90.42.070. (5)(a) Pending applications for new water rights are not entitledto protection from impairment, injury, or detriment when an applicationrelating to an existing surface or ground water right is considered. (b) Applications relating to existing surface or ground waterrights may be processed and decisions on them rendered independently ofprocessing and rendering decisions on pending applications for newwater rights within the same source of supply without regard to thedate of filing of the pending applications for new water rights. (c) Notwithstanding any other existing authority to processapplications, including but not limited to the authority to processapplications under WAC 173152050 as it existed on January 1, 2001, anapplication relating to an existing surface or ground water right maybe processed ahead of a previously filed application relating to anexisting right when sufficient information for a decision on thepreviously filed application is not available and the applicant for thepreviously filed application is sent written notice that explains whatinformation is not available and informs the applicant that processingof the next application will begin. The previously filed applicationdoes not lose its priority date and if the information is provided bythe applicant within sixty days, the previously filed application shallbe processed at that time. This subsection (5)(c) does not affect anyother existing authority to process applications. SB 6734 p. 10 (d) Nothing in this subsection (5) is intended to stop theprocessing of applications for new water rights. (6) No applicant for a change, transfer, or amendment of a waterright may be required to give up any part of the applicant's validwater right or claim to a state agency, the trust water rights program,or to other persons as a condition of processing the application. (7) In revising the provisions of this section and addingprovisions to this section by chapter 237, Laws of 2001, thelegislature does not intend to imply legislative approval ordisapproval of any existing administrative policy regarding, or anyexisting administrative or judicial interpretation of, the provisionsof this section not expressly added or revised. (8) The development and use of a small irrigation impoundment, asdefined in RCW 90.03.370(8), does not constitute a change or amendmentfor the purposes of this section. The exemption expressly provided bythis subsection shall not be construed as requiring a change ortransfer of any existing water right to enable the holder of the rightto store water governed by the right.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.03 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A holder of a confirmed water right may transfer any portion of theright to another person, to additional lands, or to a different use ifthe change does not impair another water right under the procedures inRCW 90.03.380. In reviewing proposed changes that would enableirrigation of additional acres beyond the number of acres authorized bythe right or the addition of new uses to a water right, the departmentshall evaluate and determine whether the proposed change would increasethe average annual consumptive quantity of water use in comparison tothe authorized use as confirmed under the right. If the proposedchange would increase the average annual consumptive quantity of waterused under the right, the department must determine and ensure thatother existing water rights are not impaired as a result of the waterright change.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.44 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A holder of a confirmed water right may transfer any portion of the p. 11 SB 6734right to another person, to additional lands, or to a different use ifthe change does not impair another water right under the procedures inRCW 90.44.100. In reviewing proposed changes that would enableirrigation of additional acres beyond the number of acres authorized bythe right or the addition of new uses to a water right, the departmentshall evaluate and determine whether the proposed change would increasethe average annual consumptive quantity of water use in comparison tothe authorized use as confirmed under the right. If the proposedchange would increase the average annual consumptive quantity of waterused under the right, the department must determine and ensure thatother existing water rights are not impaired as a result of the waterright change.

(1) A surface or ground water right must beconfirmed by the process established in this chapter prior to change ortransfer of a water right after the effective date of this section. Ifa water right proposed for change or transfer has not been confirmed,the water right holder may choose to have the right confirmed inaccordance with section 2 of this act or by the department of ecologyor a conservancy board, except when the referee has directed the rightto the department of ecology or conservancy board under the provisionsof section 5(2)(c) of this act. (2) If the water right holder chooses to use the department ofecology or a conservancy board, the department of ecology orconservancy board shall apply the confirmation standards as provided insections 4 and 5 of this act, and shall provide a written report to thereferee detailing the water use as reported by the water right holder.The referee need not be bound by any findings in the report, and shallcomplete the confirmation process in accordance with the provisions ofsection 5 of this act. (3) The court, the department of ecology, and water conservancyboards must develop procedures to ensure that changes and transfers towater rights are not delayed during the confirmation process. (4) When evaluating water rights for the purpose of change ortransfer of the right, the department of ecology shall rely on thequantity as confirmed by the referee. (5) Prior to the appointment of a referee for a watershed, waterright changes and transfers issued by the department of ecology or SB 6734 p. 12 local water conservancy boards and new certificates for permitted waterrights must be annotated to indicate that confirmation of the quantityof the right will be conducted upon appointment of a referee. Uponappointment of a referee, the department of ecology will submit copiesof all water right change decisions and certificates for new waterrights issued since the effective date of this section to theappropriate referee for independent review and confirmation of thequantity of the right.

The provisions of this chapter do not applyto surface water rights and claims already undergoing adjudication inthe Yakima basin for which final orders or conditional final ordershave not yet been issued. However, surface water rights and claims forwhich final orders or conditional final orders have been issued aresubject to the provisions of sections 6, 7, 9, 10, and 11(4) of thisact and RCW 90.03.380 and 90.14.140, and with respect to quantity areequivalent to rights confirmed under the provisions of this chapter.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.03 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: For water rights that have previously been confirmed as to quantityunder sections 4 and 5 of this act, and have not been abandoned undersection 6 of this act, a court conducting a water rights adjudicationshall adopt the previously confirmed quantity. For water rights thathave not been confirmed as to quantity under sections 4 and 5 of thisact, the court shall review and establish the valid quantity of theright based on the standards and requirements of sections 4 and 5 ofthis act. For rights that cannot be quantified based on beneficialuse, the court shall apply legally applicable standards.

Section 13 of this act applies to allcauses of action commenced on or after the effective date of thissection, regardless of when the cause of action arose. To this extent,section 13 of this act applies retroactively, but in all other respectsit applies prospectively.

The following acts or parts of acts areeach repealed: RCW 90.14.130 (Reversion of rights to state due to nonuseNotice by orderRelinquishment determinationsAppeal) and 1987 c 109s 13 & 1967 c 233 s 13; RCW 90.14.160 (Relinquishment of right for abandonment orfailure to beneficially use without sufficient causePrior rightsacquired through appropriation, custom or general adjudication) and1981 c 291 s 1, 1979 ex.s. c 216 s 5, & 1967 c 233 s 16; RCW 90.14.170 (Relinquishment of right for abandonment orfailure to beneficially use without sufficient causeRights acquireddue to ownership of land abutting stream, lake, or watercourse) and1967 c 233 s 17; RCW 90.14.180 (Relinquishment of right for abandonment orfailure to beneficially use without sufficient causeFuture rightsacquired through appropriation) and 1987 c 109 s 101 & 1967 c 233 s 18; RCW 90.14.190 (Water resources decisionsAppealsAttorneys'fees) and 1987 c 109 s 14 & 1967 c 233 s 19; RCW 90.14.200 (Implementation and enforcement of chapter SB 6734 p. 16 Proceedings under RCW 90.14.130 deemed adjudicativeApplication of RCWsections to specific proceedings) and 1989 c 175 s 180, 1979 ex.s. c216 s 6, & 1967 c 233 s 20; RCW 90.14.210 (Chapter applies to all rights to withdraw groundwaters) and 1967 c 233 s 21; RCW 90.14.215 (Chapter not applicable to trust water rightsunder chapter 90.38 or 90.42 RCW) and 1991 c 347 s 14; and RCW 90.14.230 (Rules and regulations) and 1987 c 109 s 102 &1967 c 233 s 23.
Nothing in this act may be interpreted oradministered in a manner that impairs or diminishes a valid waterright, including rights established under state law and rightsestablished under federal law.
Sections 1 through 7, 11, 12, 17, and 19 ofthis act constitute a new chapter in Title 90 RCW.

If any provision of this act or itsapplication to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to otherpersons or circumstances is not affected.
